summary:
SL-068 changes documentation only, plus one standalone check script: docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md (new), two added lines in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md, and tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 (new). CodeGraph shows 0 changed functions and 0 affected flows. Nothing under src/, no existing test and not .taad/fitness.yaml changed. Fitness op=check: all 62 rules hold.

What I ran:
- `SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 -Case All`: exit 0, every check held.
- The default Core suite (no filter, no -c): exit 0, 381/381. The trx shows ScanStoreRollupTimingTests ran in it as "Debug build", slowest read 30.07 ms. That confirms the trip wire runs unattended, in Debug.
- The 34 ScanStore/ArchitectureRules tests in Release: exit 0, 34/34. Release reads were 8.85-10.69 ms.

What I verified directly:
- Every file:line the doc cites: SL-042 design-slice-29.json:58 and :136-138, SL-044 doc :17-19 and :127-130, fitness.yaml :504/:541/:551, ScanStore.Rollup.cs:50-76, FolderTreeNode.cs:147.
- SL-042's ledger order: design attempt 29 at 17:23:45Z, then build attempt 1 at 23:47:34Z. No earlier stage measured the ordered read.
- The declared deviations hold:
  - T-003 really does fail an open at 500 ms or over (WindowCases.ps1:2612).
  - ChildRow(int, long, double) is 24 bytes.
  - The find text needs the moved 'and'.
  - The check script had to exist for O-003..O-010.

Two minor factual errors are left in the decision record, which is the one artifact this slice produces:
- **m1:** It says the brief's 9-40 ms was a rounding of today's runs. In fact SL-042's reflection wrote that figure two days earlier, joining SL-042's validate run and its build run.
- **m2:** It says "Nothing is kept per folder" without scoping that to the store. The window keeps an ordered row array for every folder it has opened.

Both are one-sentence fixes, and neither changes the decision. No loop: every stage on this slice ran once.

Second round: In the second round I tried to break the check script and re-read every figure the doc attributes to another source. I found one new defect, a misattributed memory figure (m3 below).

The script held up. Every reader in it either fails closed or reads formats the tree actually uses:
- Line endings: CRLF is normalised by Read-Tree, and the git blob and working-tree lines compare equal.
- Encoding: all three files are BOM-less ASCII.
- Section lookup and submitted blocks: Get-Section takes the first `## ` prefix match. Get-Submitted needs exactly two 4-space-indented lines, so a tab or fenced block fails rather than passes.
- Numbers: they are parsed with InvariantCulture. That matters on this en-IN machine, which prints '1,00,000'.
- Fitness globs: fitness.yaml's files globs are all single-line, with no braces or lists, so ConvertTo-GlobRegex reads them correctly.
- Trait regex: it matches the project's own `[Trait("Network", "TEST-NET-1")]` convention.
- -Case: it is validated. Run lowercase ('c-004') from %TEMP%, the case resolves the repo and passes, exit 0 on pwsh 7.6.6.
- Silent passes: the ones left need inputs the doc does not contain (an en dash, a wrapped or lower-cased stand-in, a 'Run 4' without parentheses). None is worth filing.

**m3:** doc :70-71 credits the 136 MiB of headroom to "SL-042's spike". SL-042's ledger has no spike stage. The only source of the figure is SL-042's reflection, which puts it on the earlier spike's throwaway layout and adds that SL-042 then spent 96 MiB of retained memory. So the doc's reversal-cost sentence quotes a headroom that is misattributed and already partly spent. The design's own wording ('~136 MiB headroom SL-042 measured') shares the misattribution.

findings.claim: The decision record says where the brief's '9-40 ms' came from, and gets it wrong. It says 'The slice's brief rounded this to 9-40 ms, but run 1's cold read was 44.12', where 'this' is the range of Runs 1-3, all measured on 2026-09-28. The brief is older than those runs. SL-042's reflection wrote it on 2026-09-26 by joining two SL-042 runs from different stages: validate's 9.16-9.80 ms and the build's 35.9-40.2 ms. So the record misstates a figure's origin on exactly the case the design marked material (C-004: 'the doc's numbers must equal the recorded test output and name their harness'). The joined range is also the kind of merge the record says it avoids. The C-004 check cannot catch this, because it only checks that '9-40' appears on a line containing 'brief'.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:41-42. .taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:74 ('The 100,000-child read measured 9-40 ms'), dated 2026-09-26T00:34Z in SL-042's ledger. .taad/slices/SL-042/validate-slice-1.json:32 (Release reads 9.16-9.80 ms). docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md:88 (35.9 to 40.2 ms). tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1:288-289.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence at :42 with: 'The slice's brief says 9-40 ms, taken from SL-042's reflection, which joined SL-042's validate run (9.16-9.80 ms, .taad/slices/SL-042/validate-slice-1.json) and its build run (35.9-40.2 ms). The runs above reach 44.12, so this record quotes 9-44.'

findings.claim: The Memory bullet says the ChildRow[] is dropped by 'the caller ... once it has built its rows. Nothing is kept per folder.' That holds for Core, but the only caller keeps an ordered copy. FolderTreeNode.EnsureChildren builds a FolderTreeNode[] in ChildrenLargestFirst order and keeps it for the life of the session, and later opens reuse it. T-003's opens 2-5 are 'warm, reusing them'. The record goes on to say a stored order in live refresh 'has to be maintained under concurrent scan writes, which nothing here measured'. A reader of that work would be told nothing holds a per-folder order, when the window already does, and those arrays are what a refresh would have to invalidate.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:58-59 and :75-79. src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTreeNode.cs:138-158 ('Later calls ... do nothing'; `Children = nodes`). tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:2611 (warm opens reuse rows).
findings.fix: Scope the sentence: 'Nothing is kept per folder in the store; the folder tree keeps the rows it built for each folder it has opened, in that order, until the session ends.' Optionally, name those kept arrays in the live-refresh item of Not covered.

findings.claim: The Decision section prices the reversal against "the about 136 MiB of headroom SL-042's spike measured". SL-042 ran no spike: its ledger has design-slice 1-29, critique, critique-review, build, code-review, validate and reflect, and no spike stage. The only source of 136 MiB is SL-042's reflection. It says the figure is the earlier spike's headroom 'on a throwaway layout', and that 'this slice spent 96 MiB of retained memory'. The doc therefore credits the figure to the wrong source. It also presents as available a headroom the as-built store has already largely spent. That is the number a reader weighing a stored per-folder order would size against. Its own Not covered item disclaims only the 699/572 figures, not this one.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:70-71. .taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:84 ('The spike's 1 GiB private-bytes verdict was on a throwaway layout with about 136 MiB of headroom, and this slice spent 96 MiB of retained memory'). .taad/slices/SL-042/index.json has no spike stage. A grep of the tree finds no other origin; fitness.yaml:219 and :500 only repeat the number.
findings.fix: Replace "paid out of the about 136 MiB of headroom SL-042's spike measured" with "paid out of what is left of the memory budget (the earlier spike's layout had about 136 MiB of headroom, of which SL-042 then spent 96 MiB retained, .taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:84)".

obligations.evidence:
docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:22-25 states both facts: by git, the rule, the figures and the design record arrived together in b5c2b62; by the ledger, the rule came first. I checked both sides:
- Git: DecisionCases C-005 prints b5c2b62 for `-S 'Children are sorted on read, never stored'`, for `-S '35.9 to 40.2 ms'` and for `--diff-filter=A design-slice-29.json`.
- Ledger: .taad/slices/SL-042/index.json has design attempt 29 at 2026-09-25T17:23:45.832Z, and no build, spike or measurement before build attempt 1 at 23:47:34.087Z.
The precondition therefore holds by the ledger and not by git, and the doc says exactly that. Formally this is owed to validate-slice.

I ran `eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests` with no filter and no -c: exit 0, 381/381. The trx records ScanStoreRollupTimingTests...UnderAQuarterSecond as Passed, with output 'Debug build ... slowest 30.07, budget 250'.
The test file has no [Trait] and no Skip. The csproj default filter is Network!=TEST-NET-1&Network!=SMB-LOOPBACK&Cloud!=CF-SYNC-ROOT. Directory.Build.props, the csproj and eng/dotnet.ps1 set no Configuration.
The doc at :95-101 says a default run is Debug and that only Release counts. Formally this is owed to validate-slice.

docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:105-108: 'Status: **not applied**', and the section is labelled 'the text submitted for the edit, not a copy of the record'. git status and C-008 show no architecture-record file was added. A git grep for 'No child order is stored' finds only the doc and the check script.

Doc :110-119 gives an exact find/replace, applied only when the find text occurs exactly once, and otherwise 'apply nothing and report the text found'. DecisionCases.ps1:186-224 feeds four lines: the handed line, an already-edited line, a reworded line and a doubled line. The replace text does not contain the find text, so the edit cannot apply twice. C-002 passed when I ran it.

docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md:128 is the pointer, after a blank line 127. At base 6566536, line 126 ends the m9 paragraph and line 128 was the next heading. C-003 checks numstat '2 0', lines 1-127 byte-identical and the rest shifted by two. It passed when I ran it.

Doc :36-38 lists the reads exactly as recorded: Runs 1 and 2 from the build check, Run 3 from the build. The range at :41 is their min/max. SL-042's 35.9-40.2 ms and SL-044's 97.9/47.5/141.9/44.0 ms each sit in their own item and match their sources (I read SL-044 doc :127-130 and SL-042 doc :88). One inaccuracy remains: the brief's 9-40 is attributed to these runs (finding m1).
Doc :22-25 says 'in the same commit by git's' clock. C-005 branches on the real git result and passed. See O-001 for the git and ledger facts I checked.

Doc :95-101 states there is no Trait, quotes the default filter, and says the default run is Debug and only Release counts. My default run confirmed all of this. Doc :88-91 says T-003 checks the 500 ms open outside dotnet test, and WindowCases.ps1:2612 confirms it.

Doc :73-79 has a '## Not covered' section naming live-refresh re-sorting and citing SL-044 doc :17-19, which I read: 'median 84 ms against 50, a UI gap of 866 ms against 250'. Decision :69 limits the closure to a completed store. The submitted engine sentence says nothing about refresh.

HEAD 6c7b843 plus the tree touch only the two docs, tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 (a declared deviation) and .taad/slices/SL-068/*. Nothing changed under src/ or in .taad/fitness.yaml. Fitness check: 62 rules hold. No fitness files glob reaches docs/design. After the edit: default suite 381/381, Release ScanStore/ArchitectureRules 34/34.

cases.evidence: The shape, no write path, is the current real state. DecisionCases.ps1 C-001 (:162-182) asserts the doc's 'not applied' status, the submitted-text label, and that no other file carries the new sentence or architecture record. The builder mutated the status to 'applied' and the case failed, and the check at :169 would fail on that mutation.

C-002 (:186-224) feeds an already-edited line, a reworded line and a doubled line into Invoke-SubmittedEdit. That function is the script's own model of the documented procedure, not the engine's editor, so the case proves properties of the submitted text rather than of the engine. Those properties are: the find text occurs once in the handed line, the replace excludes the find, and the doc states the rule. The $handed line is typed into the script. I could not check it against the engine record, which is not visible here.

C-003 (:228-254) reads the base file and checks that line 126 ends its paragraph, that line 127 is blank and line 128 a heading, numstat 2 0, lines 1-127 byte-identical, and the rest shifted. That would catch a pointer landing inside a paragraph.

C-004 (:258-305) parses the listed reads and checks the stated min/max, the margin and the rounded engine figure. It checks SL-044's figures against its doc lines 127-130, and that no range spans both harnesses. It cannot detect that the brief's 9-40 is misattributed to these runs (finding m1).

C-005 (:309-344) runs git log -S for the rule and the figures and --diff-filter=A for the design record. The real result is the same commit (b5c2b62), which is the named shape, and the case asserts the doc says so. It also cross-checks the ledger times against .taad/slices/SL-042/index.json.

C-006 (:348-389) scans the timing test for [Trait] and Skip, reads the csproj default filter, and checks that no file sets a default Configuration. My own default suite run, whose trx shows the test ran as 'Debug build', feeds the real shape independently of the text scan.

C-007 (:393-408) checks the Decision / Not covered / What reopens it order, the live-refresh item with 84 vs 50 and its citation, and SL-044 :17-19. It also checks that the submitted line has no refresh wording.

C-008 (:417-442) collects the paths from the SL-068 commits plus the uncommitted tree, and checks them against an allow-list. It checks that no fitness glob reaches either doc and that nothing in src, tests or eng names either doc. The builder planted a file under src/ and the case failed. The one path under tests/ is the script itself (declared).

Not owed by this slice; ChildrenLargestFirst is unchanged. Ties are fed by ScanStoreRollupTests.cs:382-387 and :442 (two zero-size children) and by the timing test's thousands of ties. Empty folders are fed at ScanStoreRollupTests.cs:303 and :440. No test reads ChildrenLargestFirst on a single-child folder. That is a one-element sort, and the deferral reason (code unchanged) still holds.

No test feeds a slow Release run or a Debug run over 250 ms. By design this is a wording rule: doc :86-87 has 'A single slow run ... is re-run once first' and 'A Debug number does not reopen it', and C-006 checks only 'only a Release run counts toward 1'. The design's deferral reason still holds.

Deliberately not fixed here. Doc :80-82 says the 699 MiB / 572 MB figures were not re-audited, and it cites SL-042's 652.1 MiB. No check reads that item. The deferral still holds, because the slice changes no memory behaviour.

drift: The design cited the window's no-second-sort rules as .taad/fitness.yaml:513 and :547, which are 'because' lines of two rules. The doc cites three rules by their name lines, :504, :541 and :551, which I confirmed. This is a correct but undeclared change.

The check script holds a verbatim copy of the Scan Store sentence as handed ($handed, tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1:197) and the full edited sentence ($expected, :198). C-001's no-stand-in check exempts the script itself (:178). The design's 'keep no in-repo mirror' decision allowed only the decision doc's labelled submitted text. The script labels its copy 'Test input only', but this second copy was not declared.

The design asked for a decision file of 'about 40 lines'. The doc is 135 lines, including a 'Cases and their checks' table (:121-135) that repeats the script's header. Undeclared, and it does no harm.

The script checks text at fixed places in files outside the two docs its retirement note names: SL-044 doc lines 17-19 and 127-130, the exact T-003 line in WindowCases.ps1:2612, the csproj filter string, and SL-042's ledger and design record. Its header says only an edit to 'either document' retires a case. A later legitimate edit to any of those other files will turn C-004, C-006 or C-007 red. Nothing runs tests/bugs automatically, so the failure will surface only when someone runs the script.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-068/*.json (critique-1, critique-review-1, design-slice-1, build-slice-1, index.json): engine ledger records, not slice code. The only one I opened was index.json's list of attempts, via the prompt's summary.
